summary.text: Jordan is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th District, first elected in 2006, and chairs the House Judiciary Committee. A former state champion and NCAA wrestling champion, he served in both chambers of the Ohio legislature before Congress, and was the first chairman of the House Freedom Caucus. He is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Troy, Ohio, and raised in Champaign County, Ohio; graduated from Graham High School in 1982, where, according to his congressional website, he was a four-time state wrestling champion.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin (1986), where he was a two-time NCAA wrestling champion, a master's degree from Ohio State University (1991), and a law degree from Capital University (2001).
Was an assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University from 1987 to 1995.
Served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1995 to 2000 and in the Ohio State Senate from 2001 to 2006.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and took office in 2007, representing Ohio's 4th District.

Chaired the House Republican Study Committee in the 112th Congress and helped found the House Freedom Caucus in the 114th Congress, serving as its first chairman, according to his congressional website.
Served as ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee from 2020 to 2023 and has chaired it since January 2023; also serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
His congressional website lists recognition including Americans for Tax Reform's Friend of the Taxpayer Award and the 2012 Weyrich Award for 'National Legislator of the Year.'
